p: those days: When I will deliver my Church, which consists of both Jews and Gentiles.

valley of Jehoshaphat: It appears that he alludes to the great victory of Jehoshaphat, whom God used without man's help to destroy the enemies, 2Ch 20:20-26; also he is referring to this word Jehoshaphat, which signifies pleading or judgment, because God would judge the enemies of his Church, as he did there.
given a boy for an harlot: That which the enemy received for the sale of my people, they bestowed upon harlots and drink.
what have ye to do with: He takes the cause of his Church in hand against the enemy, as though the injury were done to himself.
a recompence: Have I done you wrong, that you will render me the same?

shall sell them to the Sabeans: For afterward God sold them by Nebuchadnezzar and Alexander the Great, because of the love he had for his people, and by this they were comforted, as though they themselves had sold them.
Beat your plowshares into swords: When I will execute my judgments against my enemies, I will cause everyone to be ready, and to prepare their weapons to destroy one another, for my Church's sake.
sickle: In this way he will encourage the enemies when their wickedness is completely ripe to destroy one another, which he calls the valley of God's judgment.
hope of his people: God assures his own against all trouble, that when he destroys his enemies, his children will be delivered.
through her any more: The strangers will no longer destroy his Church: and if they do, it is the fault of the people, who by their sins make the breach for the enemy.
drop down new wine: He promises to his Church abundance of graces, see Geneva "Eze 47:1", which would water and comfort the most barren places; Am 9:13.
Egypt shall be a desolation: The malicious enemies will have no part of these graces.
cleanse their blood that I have: He had allowed his Church before this to lie in their filthiness, but now he promises to cleanse them and to make them pure unto himself.
